title: test(lint): skip a vanished entry in the startup-registry corpus walk
body:
Fixes #20269
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`packages/lint/src/lint-startup-registry-verdict.corpus.test.ts`, `collectSourceFiles`: the walk no longer runs a bare `statSync` on every listed entry. It goes through a local `statListedEntry`, which is the rule `statListedEntry` in `scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs` already pins on `main` (landed with PR #20267, for #20225), spelled the same way:

- skipped: only an entry whose `stat` AND `lstat` both answer `ENOENT` (it vanished between the listing and the stat);
- still thrown: a dangling symlink, `ENOTDIR`, `EACCES`, every other code, and a missing root;
- a present entry is stat'ed exactly as before, nothing is matched by name, and there is no retry.

The file header's false-green 1 and the walker's doc now say what is true: the walk's one `catch` skips only a vanished entry and rethrows everything else, and they name what it does not cover (a listed directory that vanishes before its own `readdirSync`, a collected file that vanishes before the sweep's `readFileSync`). No other line of the file changed.

### Why `statListedEntry` and not `readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })`

1. It is the rule already on `main`, with the same spelling. Reviewers compare it with the reference in one read, and the family keeps one rule.
2. `withFileTypes` does not remove the rule. The current walk follows a symlinked directory through `statSync`, and keeping that means a stat on every symlink entry, which then needs the same vanished-entry rule.
3. `withFileTypes` moves the race inside the listing on some filesystems. On Node 22.22.2, `getDirent` (`internal/fs/utils`) answers a `UV_DIRENT_UNKNOWN` entry with an unguarded `lstatSync(join(path, name))` inside `readdirSync` itself. On a filesystem that does not report `d_type`, a vanishing entry then throws from the listing call, where no per-entry rule can reach it.

## The race, before and after

The probe is the card's own shape. `SKIP_DIRS` through `collectSourceFiles` is extracted verbatim from `git show REV:packages/lint/src/lint-startup-registry-verdict.corpus.test.ts` and transpiled with the repo's TypeScript. It is then run over the real `packages/` tree of this worktree, while a sibling process loops create and unlink of `packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_probe.mjs`. There is one walk per run and 100 runs per revision. The injected `lstatSync` counts its calls. It runs only after a `stat` answered `ENOENT`, so it is the positive control that the head runs really met the race.

| revision | runs | threw | clean runs | files per clean run | runs where the race was hit and absorbed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `3f86dc52f2` | 100 | **23**, all `ENOENT stat 'packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_probe.mjs'` | 77 | 2690 | n/a |
| head `606510b23c` | 100 | **0** | 100 | 2690 | **44** |

The head's clean runs read the same 2690 files as the base's, so no real source file leaves the corpus. Two earlier 20-run pairs agree: base 10/20 and 6/20 threw, and head 0/20 threw with 2 runs absorbed. The probe file was deleted after every run. Afterwards, `ls packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_probe.mjs` answers `No such file or directory` and `git status --porcelain` is empty. Note that `*.bundled_*.mjs` is gitignored, so the `ls` is the real absence proof.

## Tests (head `606510b23c`)

- The touched file on its own: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lint-startup-registry-verdict.corpus.test.ts` gives `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 5 passed (5)`. `packages/lint` declares no vitest projects: its `vitest.config.ts` sets only `disableConsoleIntercept`, so this is the package's single default project.
- The whole package: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` gives `Test Files 111 passed (111)` and `Tests 4268 passed | 5 skipped (4273)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` exits 0. That covers `tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`: "@objectstack/lint's test layer compiles under packages/lint/tsconfig.test.json". `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the corpus test file, and it has no debt-ledger entry, so it compiles clean.
- Dependency closure built first: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` (spec, formula, sdui-parser).
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived 52 commands at `606510b23c`. 50 exited 0. 2 are NOT MEASURED (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET), because both need the full `packages/*` build:
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` loads every package's built CJS entry;
  - `check:type-check-debt` re-measures the ledgered packages, and `@objectstack/lint` is not one of them.
  - A `*.test.ts` under `packages/lint/src` reaches no built output, so CI measures both.
  - `--ran` with exit codes: "52 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 50 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED".
  - `check:docs-transcript-drift` and `check:lean-entry-closure` went green after I built `@objectstack/lint` and the `@objectstack/objectql...` closure.
- eslint, narrowed to the one touched file: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` read 1 file with 0 errors and 0 warnings. `eslint --print-config` on that file resolves 5 rules with `parserOptions` `{"ecmaVersion":"latest","sourceType":"module"}`. There is no `project` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

## No changeset

Measured, not assumed. `@objectstack/lint` publishes `["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md"]`. After building at `606510b23c`, `statListedEntry` and `collectSourceFiles` have 0 hits in those paths, against 4 files for the positive control `findStartupRegistryVerdicts`. The PR ships nothing.

## Acceptance notes

**Family census:** `git grep -l readdirSync -- 'packages/**/*.test.ts' | xargs grep -l statSync` at base `3f86dc52f2` returns **23 files**. The card listed 9 at `4d7e740d`, and the dev had counted 12. Question A: does it walk a tree a concurrent build writes into? Question B: does a bare `statSync`/`lstatSync` run on a listed entry before a filter would drop it? Fixed only where both answers are yes.

Where the transients land, read from source: bundle-require 5.1.0's `defaultGetOutputFile` writes `tsup.config.bundled_ID.mjs` next to the config it loads. That is the package root for the 21 packages with their own `tsup.config.ts`, and the repo root for the 46 that build with `--config` pointed at the root config. No `tsup`/`vite`/`vitest` config lives under any `src/`. Vite 8.0.16 writes its bundled config under `node_modules/.vite-temp/`. `packages/cli` builds with `tsc` into `dist/`. `@objectstack/spec`'s generators write `json-schema/` and its sibling artifact dirs at the package root, never into `src/`.

1. `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/multi-value-columns.no-auto-run.test.ts` (`everyTsFile`): A no, it walks `packages/cli/src` only (B yes). Left alone.
2. `packages/cli/src/utils/console-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` (`packageSourceFiles`): A no, `packages/cli/src` only. Left alone.
3. `packages/cli/src/utils/port-contract-single-source.test.ts` (`everySourceFile`): A no, `packages/cli/src` only. Left alone.
4. `packages/cli/test/diff-usage-error-stream.e2e.test.ts` (`commandFiles`): A no, `packages/cli/src/commands` only. Left alone.
5. `packages/cli/test/json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` (`commandFiles`): A no, `packages/cli/src/commands` only. Left alone.
6. `packages/cli/test/resolve-glob-lazy-walk.test.ts`: no walker of its own. It spies on `fs.readdirSync`/`fs.statSync` to pin a product walker over a fixture. Left alone.
7. `packages/client/src/envelope-caller-census.test.ts` (`walk`): A yes, it walks the repo root. B no, because the stat sits in a catch-all `continue` and is not bare. Left alone.
8. `packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.test.ts` (`walk`): A yes, `packages/`. B no, because it uses `withFileTypes` and stats only a symlink entry. Left alone. Caveat: on a filesystem without `d_type`, Node's `readdirSync` lstat's each entry internally (see above).
9. `packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.pin.test.ts`: no walker. The hit is prose explaining its move to git's file list. Left alone.
10. `packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver-durability.test.ts`: lists and stats a temp directory it created itself, a fixed fixture. Left alone.
11. `packages/lint/src/lint-startup-registry-verdict.corpus.test.ts` (`collectSourceFiles`): A yes, `packages/`, the probe above. B yes, a bare `statSync` before the `.ts` filter. **Fixed here.**
12. `packages/metadata/src/metadata-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` (`packageSourceFiles`): A no, `packages/metadata/src` only. Left alone.
13. `packages/platform-objects/src/managed-api-method-affordance-sweep.test.ts` (`walkObjectFiles`): A yes, `packages/`. B no, catch-all. Left alone.
14. `packages/plugins/organizations/src/no-framework-dependents.pin.test.ts` (`workspacePackageManifests`): A no. It lists `packages/` and the eight group dirs one level deep, whose entries are package directories. The transients land inside a package root or the repo root, which it never lists. Left alone.
15. `packages/plugins/organizations/src/open-only-wall-acceptance.test.ts` (`workspaceManifests`): A no, the same shape as 14. Left alone.
16. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/managed-extension-fields.test.ts` (`walkObjectFiles`): A yes, `packages/`. B no, catch-all. Left alone.
17. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-owner-email-reader-census.pin.test.ts` (`sourceFiles`): A no, `plugin-auth/src` and `plugin-security/src` only. Left alone.
18. `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/transports/smtp-port-contract.test.ts` (`everySourceFile`): A no, `plugin-email/src` only. Left alone.
19. `packages/qa/downstream-contract/test/source-resolution.pin.test.ts` (`literalSpecImports`): A no. It walks its own `src/` and `test/` in a private package with no build script. Left alone.
20. `packages/spec/scripts/category-title.test.ts` (`moduleDirsOnDisk`, and a docs `walk`): A no. It lists the top level of `packages/spec/src`, and the docs walk uses `withFileTypes` with no stat. Left alone.
21. `packages/spec/src/data/api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts` (`walkObjectFiles`): A yes, `packages/`. B no, catch-all. Left alone.
22. `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key-migrate-sentence.test.ts` (`walk`, `walkMarkdown`): A no. It walks `spec/src`, `lint/src` and the published `skills/` tree (with `lstat`), and no build writes into any of them. Left alone.
23. `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts` (`walk`): A yes, `packages/`. B no, catch-all. Left alone.

Totals: 23 hits. 1 answers yes to both and is fixed here. 22 do not and are untouched. No file in `packages/cli`, `packages/core`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email` or `packages/spec` is touched.

**Observed, not acted on:**

- Five of the "B no" walkers (7, 13, 16, 21, 23) are immune to this race only because a catch-all `continue` swallows every stat error, `EACCES` and dangling symlinks included. That is the opposite failure, a silently smaller corpus. It is not this card's rule. Noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
- This PR does not cover a residual in the lint corpus walk, by the reference rule's own boundary. The scan root here is `packages/`, which is wider than the reference's. Under it, `packages/cli` tests root fixture directories at `packages/cli/tmp/` (`config-named-export-rule.test.ts`, `config-shadowed-named-export.test.ts`, `i18n-extract-check-dry-run.test.ts`, `i18n-extract-check-json.test.ts`, `i18n-extract-companion-orphan.test.ts`, `init-template-comments-self-contained.test.ts`, `scaffold-manifest-schema.test.ts`). Those fixtures carry `.ts` files that pass the corpus filter.
  - Same probe on head, with a sibling looping mkdir / write `objectstack.config.ts` / `rm -r` under `packages/cli/tmp/tmp-probe` and every collected file read afterwards, as the suite's `beforeAll` does: **9 of 40 runs threw**. 8 threw `ENOENT open` at the read. 1 threw `ENOENT scandir` on the vanished directory.
  - In 19 of 40 runs the transient fixture joined the audited corpus: 2691 files against 2690.
  - The two can overlap in time on a local `pnpm test`. In CI `Test Core`, the overlap is NOT established: `packages/cli` runs in its own sequential slice leg (`ci.yml`, `for LEG in __whole__ $SLICES`).
  - It is reported back to the family closure card, not filed.
